title: Annotatio II §.IV: Gelasius & Prosper — divine thing, yet bread/wine nature; sacrament and res
pass_a_gloss: Finally Gelasius disputing thus against Eutyches: The Sacraments, he says, which we take are a divine thing, and yet do not cease to be the substance and nature of bread and wine. To these we add Prosper, a Writer Catholic in all things, expressly teaching: that the Eucharist consists of two — the visible species of the elements and the invisible blood and flesh of our Lord (that is, the Sacrament and the thing of the sacrament) just as Christ’s person consists of God and man — Distinction 2 on consecration, chapter This is.
pass_b_english: Gelasius against Eutyches: what we take is a divine thing, yet does not cease to be the substance and nature of bread and wine.
Prosper: Eucharist = visible element-species + invisible Lord’s flesh and blood (sacrament and res), as Christ’s person is God and man.
source_text: GELASII denique contra Eutychen ita disputantis: Sacramenta, inquit, quæ sumimus, divina res est, & tamen non desinit esse substantia & natura panis & vini. His adjicimus PROSPERUM, Scriptorem per omnia Catholicum, disertè docentem: Eucharistiam duabus constare visibili elementorum specie & invisibili Dn. nostri sanguine & carne (hoc est Sacramento & re sacramenti) sicut persona Christi constat ex Deo & homine, Distinct. secunda de consecratione cap. Hoc est.
